src/gateway_core/init.py

Python · Tier A

Shared implementation for smTO gateway wrappers.

src/gateway_core/activity_public.py

Python · Tier A

Build bounded presentation copies for Gateway HTTP activity and the inspector. structural_value always removes private context and raw binary bodies; public_value applies the chosen ACTIVITY redaction policy; request/section helpers summarize prepared wire data. These helpers neither select permissions nor mutate the original request or receipt.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
sensitive_name 33 Recognize a caller-supplied lowercase sensitive field name or a shared redaction-policy secret key. This name classifier does not itself modify values.
structural_value 42 Copy presentation-safe structures, always removing underscore/private model-context fields, replacing bytes with size metadata and bounding recursive depth at 32. Unsupported objects become a placeholder. Optional credential masking is a later projection step.
public_value 63 Strip private structure and apply the selected ACTIVITY redaction policy with explicit secret values and field/query names. Return a presentation copy; this function neither authorizes execution nor changes the original receipt.
bounded_section 80 Package already-sanitized data with identity, label and byte counts. Preserve a complete native value within the bound; otherwise return a UTF-8 text preview without a partial code point. The caller must sanitize before this size-only helper.
http_request_evidence 103 Describe actual prepared request input for the inspector: parse multipart fields while replacing file bodies with metadata, summarize other binary media, and decode textual JSON/forms. Apply structural/activity projection, expose the projected query pairs and return a bounded request section without altering transmitted data.

src/gateway_core/app.py

Python · Tier A

Compose the authenticated inbound Gateway API around one GatewayService. create_app constructs service state, binds controller pairing and installs private validation, typed operation routes, job/command SSE and terminal WebSockets. The ASGI lifespan holds the state lease and owns maintenance/update startup and service teardown. Route adapters preserve receipt and failure semantics; domain providers own host effects. The exported LazyApplication delays default construction until use or attribute inspection.

Significant symbols

Construction restores service state and worker communication; ASGI lifespan separately owns maintenance/update workers and teardown. Platform facades call this factory with their settings.

src/gateway_core/archive_capabilities.py

Python · Tier A

Build sanitized archive-operation facts for Gateway capability discovery. archive_support locates allowlisted tools, caches help/info probes by executable/codec identity and returns defensive copies; parser helpers distinguish read/extract/create/verify evidence. canonical_archive_support removes untrusted extras before persistence or model projection. Missing or malformed facts stay UNKNOWN; discovery does not authorize archive execution, install tools or inspect user archives.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
canonical_archive_support 45 Copy only recognized schema/tool/format/operation facts into the public snapshot. Validate version/hash spellings, replace unsupported state values with UNKNOWN and omit raw output, diagnostics and extra fields.
archive_operation_status 84 Resolve one operation from canonical facts: an explicitly absent tool is UNSUPPORTED, while missing or unproven capability remains UNKNOWN. A known reader does not by itself establish creation or verification support.
_seven_zip 98 Parse recognized complete 7-Zip info tables and their update/create column. Reject malformed, duplicate or unfamiliar rows rather than inventing support; a format reader proves read/extract, while per-format verification remains UNKNOWN.
archive_support 209 Under a process lock, locate the six allowlisted tools and key cached probes by executable plus adjacent 7z codec identities. Recheck executable identity after probing, return a deep copy and retain absent versus unknown separately. Launcher/plugin changes hidden from these stat keys require process restart.

src/gateway_core/artifact_discovery.py

Python · Tier A

Discover candidate generated files beneath one workspace or publishable temp directory. eligible filters internal and unfinished-looking names; snapshot performs bounded no-follow traversal and returns stat metadata rather than file contents. Collector callers decide writer readiness and later verify/open/hash each candidate. A failed scan raises an artifact error so incomplete discovery cannot masquerade as authoritative deletion evidence.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
eligible 46 Exclude hidden/editor files, partial downloads, lock/database sidecars and internal directory names from automatic publication. The test is based on a name, not content inspection or proof that a writer has finished.
snapshot 60 Enumerate eligible regular files under one trusted root, returning logical names and stat revision/size/time hints. Bound traversal to 20,000 visited entries and depth 32; skip unsafe names, links/reparse points and special files. OS errors or bound failures reject the scan rather than returning a misleading complete inventory.

src/gateway_core/artifact_maintenance.py

Python · Tier A

Own only Gateway artifact caches and their associated publishable task temp. ArtifactMaintenance coordinates in-process request/stream activity, protects recorded active or recent jobs and clears eligible caches at startup or after daily expiry. Missing/offline ownership evidence defers deletion. Controller versions, private scratch and unrelated shared temp are outside this owner; no remote job is stopped by cache cleanup.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
artifact_use 91 Wrap Gateway access in maintenance activity accounting, extending that protection over iterator consumption for streaming responses. This coordinates service instances in one process, not an interprocess execution lease.
ArtifactMaintenance 118 Own startup/daily cache cleanup under a process-wide lock and activity counter. Native RAM job receipts provide surviving-writer evidence; unknown/offline ownership defers deletion instead of trusting stale SQLite.
ArtifactMaintenance.activity 154 Increment the shared active counter under the maintenance lock, touch the namespace and always decrement/touch on exit. Any active wrapped operation defers the whole cleanup pass.
ArtifactMaintenance._protected_runs 182 Read active job-hub snapshots for all known node/override roots. Protect nonterminal jobs and, during daily cleanup, recently finished jobs; missing owner hubs or missing run identity return None to defer the pass.
ArtifactMaintenance.run_once 216 Under the process-wide lock, defer for active access or incomplete ownership evidence, then remove only eligible scoped files/temp/published trees. Startup skips age checks; daily cleanup requires 24-hour inactivity. Versions directories, protected runs and private scratch survive; per-namespace failures remain counted for retry.
ArtifactMaintenance.start 277 Idempotently run the startup cleanup attempt, clear stop state and start the daily daemon loop. A deferred/failed startup pass does not prevent later maintenance.
ArtifactMaintenance.stop 295 Signal the daily loop and join for up to five seconds; this does not cancel a filesystem operation already underway.

src/gateway_core/artifact_temp.py

Python · Tier A

Stage eligible temporary output into a run artifact workspace without granting arbitrary host-file access. reference_source distinguishes managed run paths, mapped /tmp aliases and explicit legacy OS-temp references. destination_parent and stage pin directory/source identity, copy to a private partial and atomically publish a verified copy. dispatch_temp exposes bounded discovery or staging metadata; Controller registration and content hashing remain separate.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
system_temp_roots 37 List trusted operating-system temp roots for explicit legacy references. macOS additionally accepts /tmp alongside its per-user temporary directory; this does not enumerate their contents.
reference_relative 47 Check an absolute reference in the target platform's path dialect and derive a safe relative name beneath the supplied trusted root. Reject traversal or a different root without resolving any caller-controlled descendant.
reference_source 73 Choose the allowed source root and published logical name for an explicit temporary-file reference. Mapped runs interpret /tmp only within their own published directory; downgraded runs reject that alias. Legacy OS-temp references exclude instance state, scratch and workspace internals, and use a hashed reference namespace.
destination_parent 129 Create destination ancestors while pinning them against link/rename substitution. POSIX uses descriptor-relative no-follow directory opens; Windows holds handles that deny deletion and rejects reparse aliases. Yield the parent and optional dir_fd arguments, closing all acquired handles on exit.
stage 186 Promote one eligible regular file into the artifact workspace. Pin source revision and destination parents, copy to an exclusive private partial, verify size/source stability, fsync and atomically replace the destination. Matching source/staged revisions can reuse a prior copy. Clean partials on failure and return source plus staged metadata; registration on the Controller is a later step.
metadata 290 Describe the original source and staged copy with their separate stat revisions, logical name, byte size and modification time. These tokens support optimistic consistency checks; they are not content hashes or registry artifact identities.
dispatch_temp 303 Snapshot only activity temp when supplied, otherwise run temp; never crawl scratch or global system temp. Other supported temp actions delegate to the confined staging path.

src/gateway_core/artifact_workspace.py

Python · Tier A

Own the run artifact filesystem boundary used by Controller adapters and every Gateway platform. Hashed conversation/run paths separate namespaces; environment creates generated-file, scratch and temporary directories, while contained_path/open_source reject unsafe aliases. ArtifactRequest and dispatch expose setup, metadata discovery, staging and bounded revision-checked reads. Callers supply authentication and run ownership; this boundary stays active independently of optional execution guards.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
ArtifactError 30 Safe, public error; never includes a private filesystem path.
scope_key 57 Hash an opaque conversation, run or activity identity into a fixed directory component. This gives stable names without treating caller IDs as filesystem paths; it is not an authorization check.
relative_path 64 Normalize an optional artifact-workspace URI into a portable relative POSIX name. Reject empty, absolute, drive-qualified, traversal, backslash and control-character spellings before any file access.
safe_directory 89 Create the trusted root and restricted child components with private POSIX creation modes. Resolve the root once, then reject links or Windows reparse aliases in each child; filesystem errors propagate to the caller.
workspace 114 Return the run namespace beneath a conversation hash, creating its directories through safe_directory. The same run ID in a different conversation receives a different workspace.
temporary_environment 126 Build platform-native temporary-directory variables: TMPDIR on POSIX or TEMP and TMP on Windows. Return values for the child environment without changing this process's environment.
environment 135 Create run files, scratch and publishable temp directories, with optional hashed activity/receipt subdirectories. Legacy layout uses instance temporary storage; requested mapping keeps backing directories in the workspace and probes whether /tmp routing is usable. Return paths and child environment variables; directory creation and the mapping probe are side effects.
contained_path 182 Translate a logical name or an absolute in-root path to an existing workspace member. Reject every descendant symlink/reparse alias, including aliases that stay inside the root, and return the physical path with its portable logical name.
open_source 218 Yield a no-follow regular-file handle, initial stat facts and logical name inside the namespace. Windows also checks the opened handle's final path; normal exit verifies unchanged identity/metadata unless disabled. ArtifactError retains its kind; other failures become a public artifact_changed error.
ArtifactRequest 259 Define workspace setup, discovery, staging and chunk-read inputs shared by local and remote callers. Reject extra fields and bound IDs/offsets; max_bytes defaults to 64 MiB but can be supplied explicitly. Authentication and node selection belong to callers, while dispatch enforces filesystem scope.
dispatch 282 Prepare the requested namespace, then return environment, snapshot, staged-file metadata or a revision-bound base64 read. Reads enforce the requested whole-file size limit, expected stat revision and offset, transferring at most CHUNK_SIZE bytes. Source verification completes before the result leaves the context.

src/gateway_core/auth_middleware.py

Python · Tier A

Enforce controller authentication at the Gateway ASGI boundary before protected operation dispatch. Public health and bounded pairing have explicit paths; signed HTTP/WebSocket requests bind the actual target and body, replay state and runtime epoch. Verified bodies are replayed to the app under purge/policy admission, while response observations and cleanup retain context ownership. Post-dispatch failures propagate as operation outcomes rather than safe auth rejection.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
workspace_authorization 30 Authenticate Gateway HTTP/WebSocket requests before operation dispatch, with explicit public health and bounded first-pairing routes. Own upload hashing/spooling, replay acceptance, request authorization context and runtime-policy observations; the wrapped app owns actual operations.
ControllerAuthMiddleware 43 Not yet documented
ControllerAuthMiddleware.__call__ 56 Handle public health/pairing separately; otherwise verify signed headers, runtime epoch and exact body digest before consuming a nonce and attaching controller provenance. Bound HTTP body size and each receive wait, then replay verified bytes to the app under purge/policy admission. Re-raise errors once dispatched, and always reset context and close the spool so operation failures are not mislabeled as safe authentication rejection.

src/gateway_core/browser/init.py

Python · Tier A

Expose the optional deterministic Gateway browser package.

Responsibilities

Provide the package boundary for first-class browser automation.

Boundaries

Importing this module launches no process and imports no browser library.

Lifecycle

Registry and Gateway composition use this package explicitly.

State

No mutable browser state is owned by package initialization.

Security

Browser authority remains in the existing execution and Gateway boundaries.

Collaborators

Closed contracts and deterministic adapters live in package submodules.

Public surface

Submodules define the wire contract, service and backend.

@see src/gateway_core/browser/service.py

src/gateway_core/browser/dom.py

Python · Tier A

Source-owned bounded DOM projections; never accept model-supplied JavaScript.

Responsibilities

Count revisions and extract visible text/semantics without input values.

Boundaries

No network/storage/cookie APIs, callbacks to the Agent, or page HTML serialization.

Lifecycle

Security

Collaborators

src/gateway_core/browser/playwright_backend.py

Python · Tier A

src/gateway_core/cancellable_io.py

Python · Tier A

Request-owned sockets for synchronous HTTP, including TLS and response waits.

Details

Socket shutdown interrupts blocking I/O. DNS is abandoned before any socket is created if the OS resolver cannot be interrupted. No process-wide monkeypatches.
